title: A letter of the Polish exiles on King Stanisław Leszczyński's abdication, 4 February 1736 (AGAD 1/338/0/1/1401): a number-for-letter cipher read by Prabal Gupta

steps.what: The contributor transcribed the seven scans in two passes that agree on 99.1% of 2,844 tokens; each of the 23 differences was settled on the scan, and one more group was split later.

A count-matching algorithm on Polish next-letter counts deciphered 98.2% of the letter tokens on this letter alone, with no key, crib or other letter; a solver on a Polish letter model agrees with the key on 93.1% of tokens. Reading the numbers against the Polish settled the rare signs.

The decryption was read as Polish with long Latin stretches; the code groups were valued from context (125 Stanisław, 455 Augustus III, 136 and 142 Warsaw) and nine stay unread; a blind reader named the text Polish with Latin and translated about 85% of the clauses.

The contributor searched the ledger, the cards of 1397, 1402 and 1403, a text comparison with 446, 1398, 1399 and 1400, a keyword scan of Konopczyński (1909) and one web search on the names: no reading of this letter found.

Project check: the 30-sign key is one-to-one; the 491 dotted words of the cipher, decrypted with it, are 31.2% in a word list built from the letter's own clear words and about 90 function words, against at most 5.7% for 300 shuffled keys (VERIFICATION.md). No scan compared.

validation.notes: The statistical test needs a Polish letter model (lang/), whose corpus cannot be fetched from this environment, and the contributor notes his Polish model is of modern text while the letter has long Latin stretches. A word-list test against 300 shuffled keys was used instead (VERIFICATION.md); it is not the project's n-gram validation.

outcome.method_basis: Contributor's claim: the key was found from the ciphertext of this letter alone by a count-matching algorithm, with no key, crib or other letter; the project verified that the key is one-to-one and makes Polish and Latin words, but did not repeat the search.

gaps.item: nine code groups unread (145, 156, 175, 195, 289, 505, 613, 715, 5455), [?Monti] for 675 a guess, and "cza[s]" written with 12 for 21
gaps.detail: each occurs once or twice and no text fixes it

gaps.item: the signature (a flourish), so the writer and the addressee, and the year digit
gaps.detail: the scan shows no readable name; 1736 is inferred from the contents

gaps.item: a human check of the transcription against the AGAD scans
gaps.detail: szukajwarchiwach.gov.pl is not reachable from the project and the images may not be redistributed

outcome.notes: Key and reading by Prabal Gupta; checked by the project against his files and a word-list control, not against the scans. 518 of 530 cipher words read (97.7%).
outcome.fraction_read_source: Counted from reading.md: 530 words in the cipher passages (the bold text), of which 12 are holes: 9 unread code groups, 2 uses of [?Monti] and the supplied letter in cza[s]: 518 of 530 = 97.7%. About 20 further code groups are read as names from context and are not marked.

texts.label: Letter of the Polish exiles on Stanisław's abdication, 4 February 1736 (AGAD 1/338/0/1/1401)
texts.summary: An unsigned letter among the Polish exiles: France has agreed preliminaries with Vienna and an armistice and says it cannot keep King Stanisław on the throne; the courier Orlik brings it as good news and the exiles receive it in despair; they answer with two conditions, that Europe first recognise Stanisław as lawful king for life and that he call a Diet and abdicate only there; the estates refuse the haste; two lords leave for Warsaw; the writer asks what the Turks and the Khan plan.

reading_review.note: Read the decryption as Polish and Latin sentences: the cipher passages build coherent clauses that join the clear text around them; the unspaced decryption lines are normalised in the reading, and the Latin stretches and names are the contributor's working reading, not an edition.

prior.where: The card lists the letter as partly in Polish and perhaps to Branicka and offers no decipherment; the contributor found none in the ledger, the fonds cards or Konopczyński (1909).

human: Prabal Gupta transcribed the letter, ran the solver and built the reading (issue #320, repository prabal-rje/branicki-1757). The project checked the files against each other and a control; it has not seen the scans.
